definition: Guillain–Barré syndrome is an acute autoimmune inflammation of the peripheral nerves in which the immune response damages peripheral myelin and nerve roots. It often follows an infection, surgery, immunization, lymphoma, or toxin exposure and commonly causes worsening weakness, reduced sensation, and decreased deep tendon reflexes; breathing muscle weakness and autonomic problems can also occur.
